content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

{"documentId": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "title": "Q4 investor update - send list", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list", "revisionId": "1b0d9b5d65", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:41:00Z", "text": "Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

Build access
For firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.

Sheet
One row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.
"}

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Key Takeaways from the Pitch
• [PERSON_NAME_9160] was *most excited* about our *engine capabilities* rather than specific game titles.
• 
• Apple’s game categories:
• 
    ◦ *Cozy Games* → Targeting 7-25 y/o females (e.g., Animal Crossing players on Switch, Hello Kitty Arcade players).
    ◦ *Kid Games* → Under 7 years old, designed to keep kids engaged.
    ◦ *Classic Games* → Solitaire, Hearts, etc.
    ◦ *Match-3 Games* → Low adoption but good retention; Apple recognizes better F2P alternatives exist and won’t Push a match-3 subscription.
    ◦ *Puzzle Games* → Broad category with potential opportunities.
• *Where We Fit:*
• 
    ◦ We are positioned *between puzzle and classic games*.
    ◦ [PERSON_NAME_9160] is particularly interested in *Dominoes & Tri-Peak Solitaire*.
    ◦ *Solitaire is dominated by MobilityWare*, making it difficult to compete for Apple’s interest.
    ◦ However, a *custom-built Tri-Peak Solitaire or Dominoes game for Apple* would be a strong opportunity.
[PERSON_NAME_9160]’s Feedback on Our Games
• *Domino Delights*
•

Most major ad networks, including Google AdMob, Meta Audience Network, and Unity Ads, have strict policies against *incentivized ad views* and artificial engagement.
*Potential Policy Violations*
Here’s how your idea could violate various ad network policies:
1. *Incentivized Ad engagement (Against AdMob & Most Networks)*
    ◦ Google AdMob *explicitly prohibits* rewarding users for watching ads unless it’s a rewarded ad format tied to in-app content (e.g., extra lives, virtual currency).
    ◦ Your model directly incentivizes users to watch ads for real-world payouts, which is *not allowed*.
2. *Artificial engagement / Invalid Traffic*
    ◦ Ad networks analyze user engagement, and if they detect that people are watching ads only for money (not genuine interest), they may classify the traffic as *invalid* and withhold earnings.
    ◦ Clicks, impressions, and video views *must be organic*—forcing or incentivizing views creates *low-value interactions*, which networks can penalize.
3. *Revenue Share / Arbitrage Concerns*
    ◦ If you’re paying users a portion of ad revenue, some networks may see this as *ad arbitrage*—where the intent is not genuine app usage but merely generating ad views.
    ◦ Networks like AdMob *ban ad revenue-sharing schemes* that exist solely to funnel money to users.
4. *Bot & Fraud Detection Risks*
    ◦ Many ad networks use sophisticated fraud detection systems. If a large percentage of users are just watching ads to earn money, it could trigger *fraud flags* and get your account banned.
    ◦ Even if users are real, networks might still mark their engagement as *low-quality traffic* and *suspend payments*.
*Workarounds (If You Still Want Something Similar)*
If you still want a reward-based system, consider these alternatives:
1. *Use a Legitimate Rewarded Ad Model*
    ◦ AdMob, Unity, and other networks allow *rewarded ads* as long as the rewards stay within the app (e.g., coins, extra lives).
    ◦ You could design a game where *watching ads enhances gameplay* rather than directly giving real-world cash.
2. *Partner with Alternative Ad Networks*
    ◦ Some alternative ad networks (like Mistplay or OfferToro) specialize in *reward-based advertising*, but they typically *don’t allow direct ad revenue sharing*.
    ◦ Look into *GPT (Get Paid To) networks* that allow users to complete offers, surveys, and ad views for rewards *without violating policies*.
3. *Use Affiliate or Direct Sponsorships Instead*
    ◦ Instead of using standard ad networks, you could *partner with brands directly* and give users a cut of *affiliate revenue* (e.g., watching sponsored videos, completing brand challenges).
*Bottom Line*

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - /tmp/parse.py (created). It parses saved thread files, prints the headers, uses text/plain parts and falls back to stripped HTML, and truncates each body at 6000 characters.
     ```
     import json,base64,sys,re,html
     for f in sys.argv[1:]:
       d=json.loads(json.load(open(f))['result'])
       print('=====',d.get('id'))
       def dec(s): return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(s+'='*(-len(s)%4)).decode('utf-8','replace')
       def walk(p,mt):
         out=[]
         if p.get('body',{}).get('data') and p.get('mimeType','').startswith(mt): out.append(dec(p['body']['data']))
         for c in p.get('parts',[]) or []: out+=walk(c,mt)
         return out
       for m in d['messages']:
         h={x['name']:x['value'] for x in m['payload']['headers']}
         print('---',h.get('Date'),'|From:',h.get('From'),'|To:',h.get('To'),'|Cc:',h.get('Cc'),'|Subject:',h.get('Subject'))
         b=walk(m['payload'],'text/plain')
         if not b:
           b=[html.unescape(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>',' ',x)) for x in walk(m['payload'],'text/html')]
         print('\n'.join(b)[:6000])
     ```

     import json,base64,sys,re,html
     def strip(t):
       lines=t.split('\n'); out=[]

--- Wed, 3 Sep 2025 15:25:50 -0700 |From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> |To: PERSON_4420_EMAIL |Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> |Subj: Bridge Round for [SOURCE_ORG_0001]?
Hi PERSON_4420_NAME,

I’m reaching out after a recent exchange with [PERSON_NAME_41001], who noted that
our applied-AI approach looks very aligned with what you are exploring. She
asked me to reach out to you, introduce [SOURCE_ORG_0001], and see if a short
conversation would be useful.

We are kicking off a $2.5M bridge to advance our AI-driven [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine
and beta launch our Match & Slash puzzle RPG. Why this could be a strong
fit:

AI-native studio: Engine with AI at the core of design, content generation,
liveops, analytics, and UA.
Real co-creation workflows: Designers and AI working together for 10x
content velocity with a lean team.
Innovative puzzle RPG on mobile: Fast, 3D Match & Slash tuned for Western
audiences with day-one liveops.
Efficient execution: Senior global team, disciplined burn at roughly
$100K/month, rapid iteration and multiple shots on goal.

If this aligns with T-Accelerate’s investment thesis, could we please
book  30–45 minutes this week or in the next two weeks?

*Attachments and links:* our pitch deck, two short engine demos, and live
store builds below.

*Engine demos*
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Puzzle Engine: https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk
<https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Liveops Engine: https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q
<https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

*Zombie Match 3D (US stores, still in Alpha)*
iOS: https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619
<https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
Android:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US
<https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US&utm_source=chatgpt.com>

If you cannot access the builds, I can share testflight access.
Best,
Leonard
Co-founder & CEO, [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
--- Thu, 11 Sep 2025 19:56:38 +0800 |From: PERSON_4420_NAME <PERSON_4420_EMAIL> |To: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> |Cc: PERSON_3242_NAME <PERSON_3242_EMAIL>, PERSON_5203_NAME <PERSON_5203_EMAIL>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> |Subj: Re: Bridge Round for [SOURCE_ORG_0001]?
Hi Leonard,

Thank you for sending over the information about [SOURCE_ORG_0001]. I apologize
for the slight delay in my response, as I've been on a business trip for
the past few days.

I've had a chance to review the materials, and I'd like to loop in my
colleagues, Karthic and Rutik, who I believe would also find this very
interesting and relevant to our investment thesis.

We would be happy to schedule a call with you soon to discuss this further.
Please let us know your availability in the coming days.

Best,
PERSON_4420_NAME
--- Thu, 11 Sep 2025 15:37:30 -0700 |From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> |To: PERSON_4420_NAME <PERSON_4420_EMAIL> |Cc: PERSON_3242_NAME <PERSON_3242_EMAIL>, PERSON_5203_NAME <PERSON_5203_EMAIL>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> |Subj: Re: Bridge Round for [SOURCE_ORG_0001]?
Hi PERSON_4420_NAME, Karthic, and Rutik

Thank you for getting back to us. Probably the easiest thing is to pick up
a time from our calendar: https://calendly.com/leonard.hayes/45mins

If these times don't work please let us know. We are happy to
accommodate your schedule.

Looking forward to connecting with you soon.

Best regards,
Leonard

It was great chatting with you today. Per our conversation, here are the

1- The pitch deck that we used today is attached. I also added the puzzle

adapt our puzzle engine to a new casual genre.
2- We already sent a testflight invite to your email. If There are other

https://play.google.com/apps/internaltest/4700362172478489856 - let us know

If There are deliverables you need from us, please do let me know. We are

Best regards,
Leonard

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - For each thread, call mcp__hg__gmail_get_thread with thread_id "frederick.stone@harmonygames.co/<id>", user_email "me" and format "full".
   - Decode the base64url bodies, preferring text/plain, using python3. jq is not available.
   - Write /tmp/threads/<threadnumber>.txt for each thread. Every message needs Date, From, To, Cc, Subject and the decoded body.
   - Strip "On ... wrote:" quote chains and HTML/CSS. Keep forwarded content. For calendar invites, include title, time, guests and description.
   - Thread 1817715521687421486: give full bodies only for messages dated 2025-08-25 or later, and one header line for each older message.
   - Constraint (verbatim): "Read-only: do not send, modify or label anything."
   - Instruction (verbatim): "IMPORTANT to avoid context overflow: process one thread at a time, do not print decoded bodies into your conversation, and write to files. Your final reply should only list the files written (one line each with thread number and subject)."
   - The 13 threads:
     - 1817715521687421486
     - 1842285179768836773
     - 1842280132471303520
     - 1842279098258817066
     - 1842278858600251474
     - 1842278425320449096
     - 1842277859335386393
     - 1809484409903875153
     - 1841567055589252118
     - 1842473488814293664
     - 1842473372710472466
     - 1843356361309564467
     - 1844735562296076053

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Gmail thread JSON uses messages[].payload.headers and payload.body.data, with nested parts.
   - Bodies are base64url-encoded and need padding before decoding.
   - Large tool results are auto-saved as JSON, possibly wrapped as {"result": "<json string>"} or as a [{"text":...}] list. They need to be parsed twice.
   - The date cutoff uses parsedate_to_datetime.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - /tmp/proc_fs.py is written and working.
     - Usage: `python3 /tmp/proc_fs.py <json_file> <threadnum> [cutoff YYYY-MM-DD]`.
     - It unwraps the [{"text"}] or {"result"} wrapper or an inner JSON string.
     - It walks parts recursively, preferring text/plain, then stripped HTML, then the snippet. It appends a [Calendar] section built from text/calendar (SUMMARY, DTSTART, DTEND, ATTENDEE, ORGANIZER, DESCRIPTION, LOCATION).
     - It cuts the body at an "On ... wrote:" line or a line starting with ">", unless a "Forwarded message" or "Original Message" marker has already appeared.
     - Messages older than the cutoff get a single "[older] Date | From | Subject" line.
     - It writes /tmp/threads/<num>.txt and prints only "num | subject | N msgs".
   - /tmp/threads/1817715521687421486.txt has been written.
   - Saved JSON for that thread: /home/agent/.claude/projects/-app/2c162dee-76ac-4d72-a909-66c5467177c9/tool-results/mcp-hg-gmail_get_thread-1793663258176.txt
   - Leave these unrelated files in /tmp/threads untouched: 1823332883409810377.txt, 1842285743246816270.txt, 1844294398771200045.txt.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - The first thread's result was too large and was auto-saved to a file. I parsed the file with python3 instead of reading it into context.

5. Problem Solving:
   - For each remaining thread, fetch it. If the result is auto-saved, run proc_fs.py on the saved path. Check the saved file's thread id before using it.
   - If a result comes back inline, I still have to get it into a file for the script. Avoid echoing the bodies.

6. All user messages:
   - Only the initial task message (contents in section 1), including verbatim: "Read-only: do not send, modify or label anything."
   - System notifications about background agents are not user messages. Do NOT spawn duplicates or any new agents.

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Fetch and process the remaining 12 threads one at a time, starting with 1842285179768836773.
   - Then give the final reply listing each file's thread number and subject.

8. Current Work:
   - Thread 1817715521687421486 is done: "[[SOURCE_ORG_0001] + Google] - Check-in", 21 msgs.

9. Optional Next Step:
   - Call mcp__hg__gmail_get_thread for "frederick.stone@harmonygames.co/1842285179768836773" with format "full".
   - Run `python3 /tmp/proc_fs.py <saved_file> 1842285179768836773`.
   - Continue through the list, processing "one thread at a time, do not print decoded bodies into your conversation, and write to files."

If you need specific details from before compaction (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /home/agent/.claude/projects/-app/2c162dee-76ac-4d72-a909-66c5467177c9.jsonl

--- Wed, 17 Sep 2025 14:15:12 -0700 |From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> |To: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> |Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> |Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

Great to meet a fellow ex-GREE! I have very fond memories of the 300 Berry
office, and my time There shaped a lot of my early growth in my career. I
wasn't aware that the GFR fund was associated with GREE, such a pleasant
surprise!

I booked the earliest time on your calendar. If it is helpful, I would be
happy to share an additional overview of the team, company, and roadmap
ahead of our chat.

If you also have the bandwidth, please check out our innovative new Puzzle
RPG, Zombie Match iOS alpha:
https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619

Looking forward to our conversation,

Best,
Leonard

Talk to you in a while!

Best regards,
Leonard

--- Tue, 30 Sep 2025 18:41:38 -0700 |From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> |To: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> |Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> |Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

It was great chatting with a top 200 Pokémon player and investor today and
learning about the GFR fund. Per our conversation, I wanted to follow up
with one request and two supplementary materials:

   1.

   *Next games:* [PERSON_NAME_0054] will expand on this, but I wanted to share the
   material I mentioned earlier about our puzzle engine capabilities and the
   game genres we can move into quickly. Please see the attached puzzle engine
   roadmap doc.
   2.

   *Engine strategy:* You asked about our engine strategy. I’m sharing our
   long-term vision deck on that front. Happy to go deeper into what the
   next-generation AI-powered publisher will look like in a follow-up meeting.
   This deck is separate from our main pitch not because of a lack of
   ambition, but because we recognize that building successful games first is
   essential to continuing our engine development. In the near term, we’re
   prioritizing what helps us move faster.
   3.

   *Access to Zombie Match:* What’s your email address so I can add you to
   our Google Play account? Zombie Match is available in the US App Store, but
   if this download link doesn’t work, please share your email:

   [URL_11306]

Looking forward to hearing from you next week.

Best regards,
Leonard

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).

We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.

Best,
Leonard

Hi PERSON_2574_NAME,

Thanks again for the time and the sharp questions earlier this week - we
found the discussion genuinely useful. We were a bit underprepared to
summarize our takeaways from Domino Delights on the call, so I’m sending a
clearer follow-up below and highlighting a few points that I wanted to get
across.

*Why we’re excited about LVP*
We know this market is hard. We’re looking for a lead who believes an
*engine-first &
multiple-shots at goal approach* can unlock scale; we simply didn’t raise
enough last time to fully lean into it. We also know you guys are awesome
and can really support us in our journey beyond capital injection.

*Try the current build*
We pushed an update yesterday (levels *100 → 200* plus major technical
fixes) and are gearing up for *beta-2 build*. We have 3 major features and
some polish shipping next Friday and will follow up with hopefully some
exciting KPIs, especially around playtime.

   -

   iOS: https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619
   -

   Android:
   https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US

*Partnerships & roadmap*
We’re leaning into publisher/partnerships to expand capability. Next week
we have an engine deep-dive with a potential partner and will draft a
3-year engine roadmap - what [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine looks like with 10+ engineers,
Unity plugins/SDK, and a platform that operates as a growth machine. We’ll
share those notes with you to inform your process.

*Domino Delights Learnings*

*Don'ts*

   -

   Ship innovations that conflict with the game’s natural audience or theme.
   -

   Over-commit to features with unproven incremental value (e.g., saga map,
   heavy hero animations).
   -

   Build without a strong core-game engagement loop. (This is key and why
   we moved on to Zombie Match 3D)
   -

   Over-iterate on supporting mechanics (mini-games) at the expense of the
   core. - we lost too much time for unproven mini-games and mini-games act
   more like a multiplier to engagement rather than additive so don't do
   mini-games before core is Proven
   -

   Create mismatches between hero progression design and scoring mechanics.
   -

   Interrupt new players with long, text-heavy tutorials.

*Do's*

   -

   Invest in the tile/level engine; create puzzles algorithmically to scale
   core co[USERNAME_6805].
   -

   Build *reusable* LiveOps features and tools that complement the core
   game.
   -

   Stick with Proven core mechanics; apply small, audience-aware tweaks -
   especially for change-resistant segments.
   -

   Choose an art style aligned with the target audience’s preferences.
   -

   Introduce new mechanics gradually if the audience is change-resistant.
   -

AI-native studio: Engine built with AI at the core of design, content

opex, rapid iteration and multiple shots at goal.

--- Thu, 4 Sep 2025 12:39:19 -0400 |From: PERSON_2173_NAME <PERSON_2173_EMAIL> |To: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> |Cc: frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> |Subj: Re: GRx Feedback

--- Thu, 4 Sep 2025 21:50:45 -0700 |From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> |To: PERSON_2173_NAME <PERSON_2173_EMAIL> |Cc: frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> |Subj: Re: GRx Feedback
Hi PERSON_2173_NAME,

Great to hear from you. Yes, the engine has always been the core focus.
Mobile hits are inherently hit-or-miss, so our strategy is to create
multiple shots on goal. The engine lets a lean team stand up new concepts
quickly, iterate fast, and carry forward what works.

On cadence: 4-5 months is the right ballpark for getting a new title to
playable/soft launch if Zombie Match’s alpha metrics do not meet our
targets. If Zombie Match hits, we’ll double down and scale it. If it does
not, we’ll move the next title into the pipe without losing momentum.

We’re still very much a game studio at heart and aim to build the best
puzzle RPGs in the world. Longer term, the engine also opens up second- and
third-party opportunities, but near term our focus is our own titles.

Hope this helps. Let me know if you have any other questions.
Best regards,
Leonard

Hi PERSON_0491_NAME,

I wanted to check in and see where things stand on your side. On our end,
conversations with other VCs and companies are moving along. Given the
limited time left in the year, it would be good to know where your head is
at and what next steps could look like. Could you please give us clarity on
your timeline?

By the way, we spoke with the Metaplay team yesterday to get a sense of
engine competition. Their backend solution is very robust. They offer all
the basic stuff we are offering today like leaderboards, event and
inventory management, customer support plus some more around player/guild
specific controls and discovery tools.

Their strategic decision of keeping their engine game-agnostic means they
haven’t built feature-specific client-side libraries. It’s a strong
server-side data management tool, but we believe a studio like ours can do
better by reducing dev cycles with a client-side library of drag-and-drop
events across casual titles. We surely can afford to be more specific since
our goal together would be building a billion dolllar casual mobile studio,
rather than building any genre on mobile.

Looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,
Leonard
